title: Actual section of a normalized underlying finite adjunction unit
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, b a tower base, f:X to Y a scheme morphism, and g a Geometry for f [def-sp-tower-shriek-data]. Fix a coefficient index n, a target coefficient sequence B',tau' identified with the canonical sequence, and a system pull functor F identified with g.pull. Let q package a finite module pull functor, push functor and adjunction, with a heterogeneous equality to the canonical constant-ring adjunction package. Let cF identify evaluation after F with finite pull after evaluation and be heterogeneously equal to g.ordinaryPullEvaluation. Let e and d identify the underlying finite pull and push functors with the topos inverse and direct images [def-coef-semilinear-geometry-base]. Assume the underlying finite unit followed by d and direct image of e is the topos unit, and d acts identically on sections. For every source system M, chart U over Y and x in M_n(U), the topos unit section of x transported by e.inv and cF.inv is heterogeneously equal to sectionAdjoint of the identity of g.pull(M) applied to x [def-sfb-tower-class-section-adjoint].

source.place: clause (2), finite unit and tensor maps and their transposes

proof.text: Eliminate the specified coefficient, transition, pull-functor, finite adjunction package and pull-evaluation equalities. Evaluate the underlying unit equation on x. Use the identity-on-sections property of d, then cancel e.hom by applying e.inv; this identifies the transported topos unit with the finite module unit. Apply tensorComparison_adjoint_evaluation to the system identity. Expand its finite transpose using homEquiv_unit and compose the resulting section equalities with cF.inv. This identifies the transported section with sectionAdjoint of the identity, including empty charts and zero modules.

proof_origin.place: Clause (2); complete Lean proof of the finite tensor and adjunction coordinate step.
